summary:
The **Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025** (Pub. L. 119-76) amends Titles 11 and 28 of the United States Code to restructure chapter 7 trustee compensation, adjust chapter 11 quarterly fees, and extend temporary bankruptcy judgeships.

### Trustee Compensation and Fund Allocation
Section 3(a) amends 11 U.S.C. § 330(b)(1) to increase the statutory compensation paid to chapter 7 trustees from $45 to $105 per case, and repeals 11 U.S.C. § 330(e). 

Section 3(b) directs that the remainder of the filing fees collected under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(1)(A), after paying the § 330(b)(1) trustee compensation, be deposited as follows:
*   $63.51 into the Treasury special fund established under 28 U.S.C. § 1931;
*   $25.00 into the special fund established under section 10101(b) of the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005 (28 U.S.C. § 1931 note); and
*   $51.49 into the United States Trustee System Fund established under 28 U.S.C. § 589a.

Section 3(c) amends 28 U.S.C. § 589a(b)(1)(A) by replacing the allocation of "40.46 percent of the fees collected" with a flat "$51.49 of the fees collected in each case." It also amends 28 U.S.C. § 589a(f)(1) by striking subparagraphs (B) and (C), redesignating subparagraph (D) as (B), and changing a priority reference from "Fourth" to "Second."

### Bankruptcy Fees and Deposits
Section 4(a) amends 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6)(B) to extend the application of certain chapter 11 quarterly fees from a 5-year period to a 10-year period. It modifies the fee calculation formula under clause (ii) to apply "the greater of" 0.4 percent of disbursements or a rate of 0.9 percent (increased from 0.8 percent) if the United States Trustee System Fund balance exceeds $200,000,000.

Section 4(b) amends 28 U.S.C. § 589a(f) to extend the deposit period for these fees from 2026 to 2031. Section 4(c) establishes a statutory carve-out for fiscal years 2026 through 2031, directing that fees collected under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) be deposited pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 589a(f), except that $5,400,000 annually must be deposited into the general fund of the Treasury.

### Extension of Temporary Bankruptcy Judgeships
Section 5 extends the terms of specified temporary bankruptcy judgeships from 5 years to 10 years by amending:
*   Section 4 of the Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2020 (28 U.S.C. § 152 note) across subsections (a) through (f); and
*   Section 1003(b)(2)(A) of the Bankruptcy Judgeship Act of 2017 (28 U.S.C. § 152 note).

### Effective Dates and Applicability
Under Section 6, the Act generally takes effect on the first day of the first calendar quarter occurring on or after enactment (February 6, 2026). However, specific exceptions apply:
*   **Trustee Compensation (Section 3):** Applies to cases commenced under chapter 7, or converted to chapter 7 from chapters 11, 12, or 13, on or after the first October 1 occurring after enactment.
*   **Bankruptcy Fees (Section 4):** Applies to cases commenced or pending under chapter 11 on the first day of the first calendar quarter occurring on or after enactment, and to quarterly fees under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) for disbursements made in any calendar quarter beginning on or after enactment.
